record.scannerFixes: Two real scanner faults found and fixed before any count was trusted. (a) TSX generic call sites — <Autocomplete<PatientSummaryObj> — were rejected by the tag lookahead AND would have been truncated at the generic closing angle bracket, losing every prop. (b) An earlier prop reader matched against the whole raw tag, so nested props leaked into the parent: size="small" read 73 for Autocomplete when the true top-level count is 52. Both are the failure mode the build prompt warned had already occurred twice.

gaps: ROW STATE AND REAL CONTENT ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. Table/Row owns the only Hover and Selected appearance in the system but is four text cells of 180px with no way to change their number, widths or content; an instance cannot take children. Any other table must draw its rows from Table/Cell instances, and a drawn row has no State. The frame proves it: only section 5 of 12 uses Table/Row (5 instances) and 68 rows elsewhere are drawn. In production 87 of 164 cells hold a component rather than text — Typography 47, Box 37, Skeleton 20, IconButton 10, Checkbox 5, Button 5.
Table/Cell exposes one property (Text), so a cell holds one string. Half of all production cells hold something else.

No density axis. MUI sets density with size="small" on the Table; 15 of 21 production tables set it and every one sets small, while 6 take medium. Table/Cell has a padding axis but its values are MUI's padding prop (normal/none/checkbox), not density. Section 4 draws both densities by hand.
record.openQuestionRecorded: Table/Row Hover is a solid #CBDDE0 — exactly palette.action.hover, which is also primary[100] — while Selected is primary.main #004852 over white at 8% alpha. palette.action.selected is #F0EEE8, a warm cream that appears nowhere in the row, so the selected row is not drawn from the token named for it. Whether that is correct depends on MUI's own TableRow rule, which could not be read (node_modules absent). Recorded as an open question, NOT marked as a defect. The observable consequence is not in question: hovering a row signals harder than selecting it.
